newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania predicts downfall of Serbia's Milosevic.
newsitem.headline: Albania predicts downfall of Serbia's Milosevic.

text.p: Albania said on Saturday that Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's downfall was inevitable after the head of an international mission upheld opposition local election victories annulled by Belgrade.

"In my view there is only one outcome, the end of the dictatorial regime of Milosevic, the end of the last communist dictatorship in Europe...It is just a question of time," Albanian Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu told a news conference.
Shehu also urged ethnic Albanians, who make up 90 percent of neighbouring Serbia's southern Kosovo region, to protest peacefully to win what he called their national and human rights.

Belgrade stripped the Kosovo region of autonomy in a 1989 clampdown. Albania is the only country that recognises a parallel administration set up by ethnic Albanians in the province and its self-styled president Ibrahim Rugova.

Shehu was speaking after a report by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said Serbia's Zajedno (Together) coalition won Belgrade and 14 other towns in November 17 elections. The report's findings were announced by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, the OSCE mission leader.
"We hail Mr Gonzalez's declaration as realistic and democratic and one which aims to help the democratic developments and processes in Serbia," Shehu said.
"His declaration on the results of the voting was clear. We share the same opinion with him and consider the statement very important," he added.
Albanian President Sali Berisha on Friday voiced some of his harshest criticism of Serbia since coming to power four years ago, slamming the Belgrade government as savage and anti-Albanian.
He said Kosovo's two million ethnic Albanians had even more reasons than opposition activists in Belgrade to demonstrate to gain the rights and freedoms denied to them.

"It is very clear for the Kosovo people that their freedom and rights will not come as a gift from anyone and their problems will not be solved in Tirana, Belgrade or Washington, London and Paris," he said.
